articles.title: Brian Feeney, 81, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Brian Feeney for the many years of service to Foxglove Heights.
body: Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Foxglove Heights.
Brian Feeney died in June at home on Yardley Lane, at the age of 81.

Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Cedar Hollow Garden Club in his or her name. Born in Foxglove Heights in the years after the war, Brian Feeney spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.

articles.title: Budget Hearing Draws 26 Residents
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Willow Street disagreed about cost and timing.
body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. Public works estimates the work will take about 26 weeks once it starts in October.

Councilmember Angela Fairbanks asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $18,500. Residents of Eastgate said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

articles.title: Eastgate Elementary Parents Organize Senior Exercise Class
articles.deck: The program begins in October and is open to all students in grade 8 and up.
body: Students will meet on Monday afternoons in the Eastgate community hall, and transportation will be provided for those who need it. The board will review the results at the end of the fall term.
Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for October. Principal Beatrice Varga said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers.

articles.title: Council Tables Park Bench Program Ordinance
articles.deck: The vote came after 28 residents spoke at Friday’s session.
body: Residents of Lower Millrace said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. Councilmember Eleanor Zielinski asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $3,400.
Public works estimates the work will take about 28 weeks once it starts in April. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.
Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

articles.title: Letter: Support the Free Tax Clinic
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the December meeting.
Please keep the free tax clinic in the budget. Many of us on Rail Road use it every week.
Mateo Prentice, Tannery Flats
